This suit is instituted by the plaintiffs against the defendant for relief of direction to defendant quit,
vacate and deliver vacant possession suit schedule premises to plaintiffs.

Plaintiffs have also sought for damages from defendant at rate of Rs.25,000/- per month from the date of the suit, till handing over of possession of suit premises to plaintiffs and grant such other relief.

2. The case of the plaintiff in brief is as under:-

sentences.text:
That, plaintiffs have purchased suit schedule property under Registered Sale deed dated 20.05.2020 from M/s Balaji Builders, represented by its proprietor Sri. S.
Bhaskar.
On date of purchase, plaintiffs were put in possession of suit property.
Since, apartment requires some repairs, vendor S. Bhaskar has taken responsibility to complete the same.

Thereafter, he started to avoid Plaintiffs as such plaintiffs having doubted about him, they went to suit property on 2 nd Week of January 2022 after COVID Pandemic was over they come to know that, defendant is in occupation of suit property.

The plaintiff further come to know S. Bhaskar executed lease agreement in respect of suit property in favour of defendant on 19.09.2020 and put defendant in possession of suit property by receiving lease amount of Rs.20,00,000/-.
The plaintiffs have issued legal notice on 18.01.2022 calling upon defendant to vacate suit property.
Though, defendant received legal notice issued by plaintiffs but failed to comply the demand made by plaintiffs in notice.
On these pleadings, plaintiffs have prayed to decree the suit as prayed in plaint.
3. In pursuance service of the summons, defendant has tendered his appearance before the court through his counsel and filed written statement.

4. The contents of written statement of defendant in brief are as under :-
That, suit of the plaintiff is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
Plaintiffs have not filed suit properly.
Suit is bad for misjoinder of parties.
Sri. S. Bhaskar is same person who sold suit property to plaintiffs and leased out same in favour of defendant.
The plaintiffs knows that S. Bhaskar is main person for those transactions and he was not made as party to the suit.
Defendant is not aware about, plaintiffs have purchased suit property from S. Bhaskar under Registered Sale deed dated 20.05.2020.

It is specifically contended that, defendant has approached S. Bhaskar for lease of property, he being owner of suit property leased out suit property in favour of defendant for sum of Rs.20,00,000/-.
The defendant being interested in suit schedule property agreed to pay security deposits of Rs.20,00,000/- and entered into lease agreement dated 19.09.2020 with S. Bhaskar.
Defendant has taken possession of suit property from S. Bhaskar on 10.10.2020 and lease period is from 10.10.2020 to 09.10.2023.
The defendant is in lawful possession and enjoyment of suit property as per lease agreement entered between himself and S. Bhaskar.
Cause of action shown by plaintiffs in plaint is imaginary one.
The plaintiffs have filed false and frivolous suit.
On these grounds, it is requested by the defendant to dismiss the suit of the plaintiffs.

5. On the basis of above pleadings of both parties, this court has framed the following:

sentences.text: 1. Whether the plaintiffs prove that in view of they purchased the suit property under registered sale deed dated 20.05.2020 they became the landlord of defendant in respect of suit properties?
2. Whether the plaintiffs prove that they validly terminated the tenancy by issuing legal notice dated 18.01.2020 ?
3. Whether the plaintiffs prove that they are entitle for the relief of eviction ?
4. Whether the plaintiffs prove that they are entitle for damages of mesne profits, if entitle what would be the quantum ?
5. Whether?
6. What order or decree?
6. To substantiate the case of the plaintiffs, plaintiff examined himself as PW1 and got marked 7 documents as per Exs.P.1 to Ex.P.7.
Defendant examined himself as DW1 and power of attorney holder of other defendant examined himself as DW2 and got marked 7 documents as per Exs.D1 to Ex.D7.
7. I have heard the arguments of learned counsel for plaintiffs and defendant and perused the records.

8. After close scrutiny of oral and documentary evidence and after hearing the arguments, my findings to the above points are as follows:-
ISSUE No.1 - Partly in the Affirmative; ISSUE No.2 - Partly in the Affirmative; ISSUE No.3 - In the Affirmative; ISSUE No.4 - Partly in the Affirmative; ISSUE No.5 - As per final order, for the following - REASONS 9. ISSUE No.1 :-As per case made out by plaintiffs, they together have purchased suit schedule property under registered sale deed dated 20.05.2020 from Mrs. Balaji Builders represented by its proprietor Sri S. Bhaskar.

In order to substantiate same, original sale deed dated 20.05.2020 executed by S. Bhaskar as a proprietor of Balaji Builders in respect of suit property in favour of plaintiffs has been produced as per Ex.P1.
10.
It is worth to note here that, defendant is not disputing ownership of S. Bhaskar over suit schedule property.
It is only a contention of defendant that, he approached Bhaskar for lease of property.

Bhaskar who was owner of suitable property, leased out suit property in favour of defendant for sum of Rs. 20,00,000/- and consequently defendant and S. Bhaskar have entered into lease agreement on 19.09.2020 in respect of suit property.

sentences.text: The power of attorney holder of defendant, who examined as D.W.2 in his cross examination has categorically admitted, plaintiffs have purchased suit schedule property as per Ex.P1 sale deed.
It is also admitted by D.W 2 that, as per Ex.P3, concerned BBMP authorities have issued katha in respect of suit property in the names of plaintiffs.
It is also admitted by D.W 2 that, as per Exs.P4 to P9,
plaintiffs
have paid tax pertaining to suit property to BBMP.
12. Recital of Ex. P1 sale deed itself sufficient to come to conclusion, plaintiffs have purchased suit schedule property under Ex.P1 registered sale deed from M/s Balaji builders.
It is specific contention of plaintiffs that, they become landlord of defendant in respect of suit premises.

13. It is argued on behalf of learned counsel for plaintiffs that, in view of transfer of ownership of suit premises to the plaintiffs by S. Bhaskar, defendant become tenant of plaintiffs in respect of suit property.

The learned counsel for plaintiffs in support of his argument has relied upon decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka reported in 2004 LAWS (KAR) 9 38 in case of Shilva Uddin v. Sri Nagaraju wherein it is held that, in India, no attornment of tenancy is necessary in law as per Section 109 of T.P.Act, which creates a statutory attornment.

entities.text: High Court of Karnataka reported in 2004 LAWS (KAR) 9 38
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Section does not insist that, transfer of lessor's right can take effect only if the tenant attorns.
Attornment by the tenant is unnecessary to confirm validity to the transfer of lessor's rights.
The transfer of ownership of premises to respondent by previous lessor has resulted in statutory attornment by tenant in favour of transferee.
14. It is material to note here that, herein the case defendant who enters possession of suit premises without consent of plaintiffs.
As such, it does not automatically establishes landlord and tenant relationship between plaintiffs and defendant.

As defendant subsequent to purchase of suit property by plaintiffs entered into possession of suit property without their consent, such possession of defendant over suit premises is an unlawful or unauthorised occupation of suit property.
15. A landlord and tenant relationship requires owner's consent and acknowledgment of owner's right, which are absent in a simple act of taking possession.
Owner must consent to the occupancy and tenant must acknowledge owner's title and right to the property.

Simply taking possession of suit premises by defendant from S. Bhaskar, who had already sold suit premises to plaintiffs does not create landlord and tenant relationship between plaintiffs and defendant.

16. It is not the case of plaintiffs that, earlier to purchase of suit property from S. Bhaskar under Ex.P1, there was a lease agreement entered between S. Bhaskar and defendant in respect of suit property.
Thereafter, by virtue of Ex.P1, S. Bhaskar being the proprietor of Balaji Builders has sold suit property in favour of plaintiffs.
As such, even in absence of acknowledgment by defendant, there is an automatic attornment of tenancy in respect of such property by defendant.

17. Here in the case, S. Bhaskar, without having any right or interest over suit property and having already sold sole property in favour of plaintiffs as per Ex.P1, entered into lease agreement with defendant.
As such there is no attornment of tenancy in respect of suit property.

As defendant entered into possession of suit property without consent of plaintiffs, for all practical purposes, his possession over suit property is unlawful and unauthorised possession over suit property.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 partly in the affirmative.

5 18. ISSUE No.2 :- As already discussed, there is no land order and tenancy relationship between plaintiffs and defendant in respect of suit property.

sentences.text: Plaintiffs have produced Legal Notice dated 18.01.2022 as per Ex.P5 issued to defendant asking him to quit, vacant and deliver suitable property to them and also pay damages.
D.W. 2 in his cross examination has categorically admitted legal notice issued by plaintiffs as per Ex.P5 served on defendant.
It is also admitted, defendant has not issued any reply to notice issued by plaintiffs.

19. In the view of contents of Ex.P5 legal notice and evidence of PW1 and evidence of DW2, it can very well gathered that, plaintiffs being owners of suit property have issued legal notice as per Ex.P5 asking defendant to vacate suit property and hand over vacant possession of suit property to them and to pay damages for his unauthorized and unlawful occupation of suit property.
Hence, I answer Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.

20. Issues No.3 and 4 :- As these two issues are inter-related to each other and involves common appreciation of facts and evidence on record, findings on one issue are bearing on other issue, in order to avoid repetition of facts and for convenience sake, these issues are taken together for common discussion.

21. It is pertinent to note here that, plaintiffs being the owners of suit property, they are entitled for vacant possession of suit property from defendant who is in unauthorized possession and enjoyment of same.
It is contention of defendant that, as per Ex.D1 surrender of lease dated 23.02.2024,
defendant
has already handed over possession of suit property to S. Bhaskar

It is fact that surrender of lease entered between defendant and S. Bhaskar on 23.02.2024,
which is during pendency of suit.

DW2 in his cross examination has deposed as per Ex.D1, S.
Bhaskar has returned lease amount and defendant handed over possession of suit property to S.
Bhaskar.
That is clearly admitted by DW 2 that, defendant has not informed to the court that, he is handing over possession of suit property to S. Bhaskar.
The DW.2 has pleaded his ignorance as to whether defendant has obtained permission of the court to hand over possession of suit property to S. Bhaskar or not.
23. It is worth to note here that, as per Ex.D5 defendant has lodged complaint against S. Bhaskar on 01.05.2023, which is subsequent to filing of suit by plaintiffs.

In the said complaint, it is alleged by the defendant that, S. Bhaskar has committed an offence punishable under Section 406 and 420 of IPC.
24.
As earlier discussed, DW 2 has clearly admitted in his cross examination, as per Ex.P1, plaintiffs have purchased a suit property from S. Bhaskar.
Surrender of lease as per Ex.D1 is very much subsequent to filing of complaint by defendant as per Ex.D5.
If that is so, there is no need for defendant to hand over possession of suit property to S. Bhaskar, who is not at all owner of suit property.
At the same time, on 09.04.2022 S. Bhaskar has also filed complaint.

On combined appreciation of all these facts, inference can be done that, defendant and S. Bhaskar have colluded with each other and created Ex. D1 surrender of lease.

6 25.

entities.text: Jayasheel Reddy G vs K Venkatesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is important to note here that, if document as per Ex.D1 is genuine document, defendant having aware about the rights of plaintiffs over suit property by virtue of Ex. P1 definitely informed the court that, he is going to hand over possession of suit proper to S. Bhaskar or he going to hand over possession of suit property to plaintiffs.
It can safely inferred defendant and S. Bhaskar together have created Ex.D1 surrender of lease just to not to give possession of the property to plaintiffs.
26. The plaintiffs being owners of suit property they are entitled for vacant possession of suit property from defendant, who has been in possession and enjoyment of same unauthorisedly.
It is come in the evidence of DW. 2 and same is mentioned in Ex.D1 that, S. Bhaskar has returned lease amount to defendant.
It is fact that, S. Bhaskar not being owner of such property handed over possession of suit property to defendant on lease.

It is not the case of either defendant or S. Bhaskar,
they have paid lease amount to the plaintiffs, who are actual owners of suit property.
As per contents of Ex.D1, it can be gathered.
Lease amount of Rs 20,00,000/- paid by defendant to S. Bhaskar is interest free security amount.
27. There is no material placed by plaintiffs to show they can earn rent of Rs. 25,000/- per month from suit schedule property if same was let out to some other persons.
Even there is no documents produced by defendant to say what is rent amount he agreed to pay to S. Bhaskar in the respect of sole property.
It can be gathered from Ex.D1 an amount of Rs.20,00,000/- fixed as a security deposit without interest.
28. The DW 2 has admitted that, the suit premises is 3 BHK House.
Taking into note of locality of suit property and its extent, it can be inferred that, suit schedule property may fetch an amount of  20,000/- per month as rents.

As defendant has occupied suit property unauthorisably, he has to pay an amount of  20,000/- per month to plaintiffs as damages from date of suit, till handing over of possession of same to plaintiffs.
I answer Issue No.3 in the affirmative and Issue No.4 partly in the Affirmative.

29. Issue No.5 :- In view of the above said findings on issues No.1 to 4, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The suit of the plaintiffs is hereby decreed with costs.
The defendant, who is in unauthorised possession of suit schedule premises has to quit and deliver vacant possession of suit premises to plaintiffs within one month from the date of decree.
Failing which, plaintiffs are at liberty to get vacant possession of suit schedule premises from defendant by following due procedure known to law.

Further defendant has to pay damages at rate of Rs.20,000/- per month from date of suit, till handing over of vacant possession of suit property to plaintiffs along with interest at rate of 6% per annum from date of suit, till handing over of vacant Jayasheel Reddy G vs K Venkatesh on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78598880/
7 possession of suit property to plaintiffs.
Draw decree accordingly.
